reasons: Claimed status is compliant and the finding is consistent with that: the rendered redline is byte-identical to the original paragraphs and no counterparty comment is proposed, so nothing is being raised in negotiation.

The cited text does supply a usable exit regime: Section 14.2(a)(iv) is expressly mutual ('Each Party shall use Diligent Efforts to cooperate with the other ... to effect a smooth and orderly transition ... during the Wind-down Period'), 14.2(a)(ii) supplies a defined transition runway keyed to the termination ground, 14.2(a)(iii)/(vi) provide orderly transfer of Regulatory Filings, Data and materials with a 90-day outside date, and Article XIV survives under 14.5 — enough to sit at or above the fallback on material terms.

Cost allocation is expressly addressed in 14.2(a)(i) and (iii), so transition help is not left as an uncapped fee exposure; the preferred 'return Customer Data / certify deletion' mechanic maps only loosely onto an in-licence where the licensee, not a hosting vendor, holds the data.

The failed deterministic check ('data return/transition present') is a phrasing artifact: the clause plainly uses 'Transition', 'Return of Materials' and 'smooth and orderly transition' rather than playbook SaaS vocabulary ('Customer Data', 'machine-readable'), so the regex miss is not evidence of absence.

Noted, not a basis to fail: Array has no express reciprocal obligation to return/destroy Ono Confidential Information and Data with a deletion certificate (14.2(a)(vi) runs one way), and Article IX is absent from the 14.5 survival list. The rationale correctly records these as sub-elements short of the preferred wording and routes them to the confidentiality and supply/survival rules rather than double-flagging here.
